headline: Agentic QA and evaluation practices advance: spec-driven delivery, agent experience metrics, and reusable evaluation frameworks enter QA workflows.

top_signal.title: Akka tests spec-driven AI delivery across 65 open-source projects
top_signal.summary: Akka ran a spec-driven delivery experiment across 65 open-source projects to measure how structured specs, model choice, and validation affect AI-assisted porting and test coverage, reporting measurable efficiency and quality differences across workloads. ([infoq.com](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-spec-driven-delivery/))
top_signal.why_it_matters: Shows a concrete, repeatable spec→validate workflow for agentic delivery — relevant to teams adopting AI agents for test generation, differential testing, and validation. ([infoq.com](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-spec-driven-delivery/))

items.title: What is Agent Experience (AX)? — measuring agent correctness with AX
items.summary: Microsoft’s AX guidance describes measuring how well coding agents use project tech, choose APIs, and complete tasks — including scenario-based runs and task-level metrics for agent-tool interactions. ([developer.microsoft.com](https://developer.microsoft.com/blog/tag/agent-experience/?utm_source=openai))
items.why_it_matters: AX gives QA teams concrete measurement targets (tooling compatibility, task success rates) for validating agent-driven test creation and automation. ([developer.microsoft.com](https://developer.microsoft.com/blog/tag/agent-experience/?utm_source=openai))

items.title: Pizza Bot: an open-source inbox for background AI agents
items.summary: AWS released Pizza Bot, a self-hosted inbox model for long-running background agents that preserves provenance, approval boundaries, and scheduled runs — designed for asynchronous agent work and inspection. ([aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/opensource/introducing-pizza-bot-an-open-source-inbox-for-ai-agents-that-work-in-the-background/))
items.why_it_matters: Makes background agent outputs auditable and reviewable — important for QA workflows, human-in-the-loop approvals, and reproducible failure triage of agent-driven tests. ([aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/opensource/introducing-pizza-bot-an-open-source-inbox-for-ai-agents-that-work-in-the-background/))

items.title: Grounding AI agents in contracts: empirical spec-driven test-generation results
items.summary: An empirical paper evaluates spec-driven agent test-generation against production bugs and reports a meaningful improvement in bug detection and branch coverage versus baseline test-generation agents. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17177?utm_source=openai))
items.why_it_matters: Provides evidence for spec-driven agent test generation improving defect detection and coverage — useful when planning agent-based test generation pilots. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17177?utm_source=openai))

watch.title: Akka’s 'We ported 65 OSS projects with AI' blog — follow adoption of Akka Specify / spec tooling
watch.summary: Akka’s own blog describing their porting experiment and Akka Specify highlights spec tooling, benchmark runners, and guardrails worth monitoring as spec-driven QA toolchains mature. ([akka.io](https://akka.io/blog/we-ported-65-oss-projects?hs_amp=true&utm_source=openai))
watch.why_it_matters: If Akka Specify and related spec kits gain traction, QA teams must revisit test ingestion, provenance, and adversarial validation strategies. ([akka.io](https://akka.io/blog/we-ported-65-oss-projects?hs_amp=true&utm_source=openai))

learning.title: Building Reusable Evaluation Frameworks for Agentic AI Products (Susan Chang, Elastic) — QCon talk
learning.summary: Susan Chang outlines a production-grade evaluation framework that combines programmatic metrics, LLM-as-judge patterns, and deep tracing to prevent regressions and measure factuality, recall, and tool-call correctness. Recorded at QCon AI. ([infoq.com](https://www.infoq.com/presentations/elastic-ai-agent-evaluations/))
learning.why_it_matters: Practical playbook for QA teams building repeatable agent evaluation pipelines, regression tracing, and composite metric roll-ups. ([infoq.com](https://www.infoq.com/presentations/elastic-ai-agent-evaluations/))
